'''Grace Yun Yi''' is a professor of the [[University of Western Ontario]] where she currently holds a Tier I [[Canada Research Chair]] in [[Data Science]].<ref>[https://fisher.stats.uwo.ca/faculty/yyi/ Grace Y. Yi]</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1016/j.jmva.2020.104693 | title=Dynamic tilted current correlation for high dimensional variable screening | year=2021 | last1=Zhao | first1=Bangxin | last2=Liu | first2=Xin | last3=He | first3=Wenqing | last4=Yi | first4=Grace Y. | journal=Journal of Multivariate Analysis | volume=182 | article-number=104693 | s2cid=228919597 | doi-access=free }}</ref> She was a professor at the [[University of Waterloo]], Canada, where she holds a University Research Chair in Statistical and Actuarial Science. Her research concerns [[survival analysis|event history analysis]] with [[missing data]] and its applications in medicine, engineering, and social science.<ref name="profile">[https://uwaterloo.ca/statistics-and-actuarial-science/people-profiles/grace-y-yi Grace Y. Yi] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160827164355/https://uwaterloo.ca/statistics-and-actuarial-science/people-profiles/grace-y-yi |date=2016-08-27 }}, People profiles, Statistics and Actuarial Science, [[University of Waterloo]], retrieved 2016-07-10.</ref>

==Education and career==
Yi earned bachelor's and master's degrees from [[Sichuan University]], China, in 1986 and 1989. She moved to Canada and continued her studies with another master's degree from [[York University]] in 1996, and a Ph.D. from the [[University of Toronto]] in 2000 under the supervision of [[Donald A. S. Fraser]].<ref name="profile"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=134788}}</ref> She came to Waterloo as a [[postdoctoral researcher]], and then continued there as an assistant professor in 2001.<ref name="profile"/>

==Recognition==
Yi won the CRM–SSC Prize of the [[Statistical Society of Canada]] in 2010.<ref>[http://www.ssc.ca/en/awards/2010/grace-y-yi Grace Y. Yi, CRM-SSC Prize in Statistics 2010], [[Statistical Society of Canada]], retrieved 2016-07-10.</ref>
Her work with Xianming Tan and Runze Li won the Canadian Journal of Statistics Award for 2016.<ref>[http://www.ssc.ca/en/awards/2016/grace-y-yi-xianming-tan-and-runze-li Grace Y. Yi, Xianming Tan, and Runze Li, The Canadian Journal of Statistics Award 2016], [[Statistical Society of Canada]], retrieved 2016-07-10.</ref>

In 2015 she was elected as a [[Fellow]] of the [[American Statistical Association]] "for research excellence in developing statistical theory and methods, particularly in missing and mis-measured data; for important contributions to [[biostatistics]]; and for excellence in statistical education and mentoring students."<ref>{{citation|url=http://bulletin.imstat.org/2015/10/asa-name-62-new-fellows/|title=ASA name 62 new Fellows|date=October 2, 2015|journal=IMS Bulletin|access-date=July 10, 2016|archive-date=October 31, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161031184324/http://bulletin.imstat.org/2015/10/asa-name-62-new-fellows/}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://www.amstat.org/newsroom/pressreleases/2015-ASANames62NewFellows.pdf|title=ASA name 62 new Fellows: Selection honors each as "foremost members" of statistical science|publisher=[[American Statistical Association]]|date=June 4, 2015|access-date=2016-07-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304081541/http://www.amstat.org/newsroom/pressreleases/2015-ASANames62NewFellows.pdf|archive-date=March 4, 2016}}.</ref> She is also a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://imstat.org/honored-ims-fellows/|title=Honored IMS Fellows|access-date=2020-07-01}}</ref> She was elected chair of the ASA Lifetime Data Science Section in 2021.<ref>{{Cite news|title=2021 ASA Election Results|url=https://www.amstat.org/asa/files/pdfs/2021-ASAElectionResults.pdf}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
* Cook, R. J., Zeng, L. and Yi, G. Y. (2004), "Marginal Analysis of Incomplete Longitudinal Binary Data: A Cautionary Note on LOCF Imputation." ''Biometrics'', 60: 820–828. {{doi|10.1111/j.0006-341X.2004.00234.x}}
* Lindsay, B. G., Yi, G. Y., & Sun, J. (2011). "Issues and strategies in the selection of composite likelihoods." ''Statistica Sinica'', 71–105. {{JSTOR|24309263}}
* Yi, G. Y., & Cook, R. J. (2002). "Marginal methods for incomplete longitudinal data arising in clusters." ''Journal of the American Statistical Association'', ''97''(460), 1071–1080. {{doi|10.1198/016214502388618889}} 
* Lang Wu, Wei Liu, Grace Y. Yi, and Yangxin Huang, "Analysis of Longitudinal and Survival Data: Joint Modeling, Inference Methods, and Issues" ''Journal of Probability and Statistics'', vol. 2012, Article ID 640153, 17 pages, 2012. {{doi|10.1155/2012/640153|doi-access=free}} 
* Cook, R. J., Kalbfleisch, J. D., & Yi, G. Y. (2002). "A generalized mover–stayer model for [[panel data]]." ''Biostatistics'', ''3''(3), 407–420. {{doi|10.1155/2012/640153|doi-access=free}}
